chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his fathers (peace be upon them):

That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked: 'How does the amputee perform Istilam (kissing/touching the Kaaba stone)?' He said: 'He performs Istilam of the Stone from the point of amputation. If the arm is amputated from the elbow, he touches the Stone with his left hand.'

key_terms.الْأَقْطَعُ: The amputee (one who has lost a limb)

ai.seo_question: How does an amputee perform Istilam of the Hajar al-Aswad during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fiqh of Istilam for the amputee (al-aqta'), specifying that the touch originates from the point of severance, with a specific instruction to use the left hand if the amputation is at the elbow. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adapting ritual purity and worship to physical realities, ensuring the act remains valid despite anatomical changes. The ruling underscores the principle that the intention and the remaining functional limb suffice for fulfilling the Sunnah of touching the Black Stone.
